grid.comment: All components snap to this grid. x/y are zero-based cell coordinates; w/h are spans in cells.

rules.description: SAY: every dashboard carries exactly one title in the top row (y = 0) stating the message, not just the subject.
Components must lie fully inside the grid.
Components must meet their type's minimum width/height so the rendered view stays legible.
Every chart-class component (bar, line, area, scatter, table, map) carries a non-empty, message-style title.

UNIFY: every data-bearing element declares its IBCS scenario (actual, plan, forecast, previous year or delta) so a reader never has to guess whether a value is actual or planned. Mark it via the component's Scenario (IBCS) prop.

EXPRESS: choose the chart type that fits the analytical message — development over time uses columns or lines, comparison and deviation use bars, structure uses bars or a table, correlation uses a scatter. Declare the message via the component's Message (IBCS) prop.

CONDENSE: maximise information density — an IBCS report fills at least 45% of the canvas with content rather than leaving wasteful whitespace. Increase density (small multiples, tighter layout) instead of spreading a few elements across empty space.
STRUCTURE: headline scenario figures (KPIs) read above the analytical charts — the summary leads, the detail follows, top to bottom.
